projects.title: SPECTER
projects.subtitle: Post-Quantum Stealth Addresses • Ethereum • Sui
projects.description: Post-quantum stealth address protocol for Ethereum and Sui. Pay any ENS (.eth) or SuiNS (.sui) name and SPECTER derives a fresh, unlinkable one-time address for every payment, secured by ML-KEM-768 (NIST FIPS 203). Ships with a TypeScript/WASM SDK on npm, a hosted API, an in-browser playground, and private trading on Yellow Network.
projects.longDescription:
Onchain payments today are fully transparent: every transfer exposes both sender and recipient. SPECTER fixes this. A recipient publishes one public meta-address (linked to their ENS or SuiNS name), and every sender derives a different one-time stealth address for each payment. Only the recipient can discover and spend those funds; to everyone else they look like transfers to random addresses.

The discovery path uses ML-KEM-768 (NIST FIPS 203), a lattice-based post-quantum KEM, so announcement data stays private even against "harvest now, decrypt later" quantum adversaries. One-byte view tags let recipients skip ~99.6% of announcements, scanning 80K announcements in about 1.5 seconds.

SPECTER is more than a hackathon demo. It ships as a full stack: a Rust/Axum backend and hosted API, a React web app (Setup → Send → Scan), the @specterpq/sdk TypeScript SDK compiled to WebAssembly so all cryptography runs on-device, an interactive SDK playground, a self-custodial "I don't trust SPECTER" recovery flow that works even if SPECTER goes offline, and a Yellow Network integration for anonymous state-channel trading. Started at ETHGlobal HackMoney 2026, won 3rd prize at the ETHCC[9] stage pitch, and selected for Founder School Cohort 2.

Pay human-readable names: ENS (.eth) on Ethereum and SuiNS (.sui) on Sui

projects.title: TuckBack
projects.subtitle: AI Reminders • On-Device Intelligence • iOS
projects.description: A private, local-first AI reminder app for iPhone. Type, speak or snap an unfinished thought; on-device AI understands the date, person and promise, then brings it back at the right moment with one clear next step. Built in Swift 6 with Apple Foundation Models, deterministic grounding and an opt-in cloud challenger. Live in public TestFlight beta.
projects.longDescription:
To-do apps optimise the list. TuckBack optimises what it feels like to carry your life. You tuck a thought away (by text, voice, camera or scan, in English, Hindi, Hinglish, Spanish or German) and it leaves your attention. It returns when it can actually move, in your own words, with who it involves and one grounded next step instead of a wall of options.

The AI is designed around one rule: models propose, code decides. Every capture is committed to an on-device SQLite database before any model runs, so an AI failure can never lose a thought. A deterministic interpreter and forty versioned Action Recipes always produce an answer. Apple Foundation Models (iOS 26) can refine it on-device, and an opt-in OpenAI or Gemini second opinion can compete, but every proposal passes the same grounding validator and confidence policy. Ungrounded people, times or amounts, unsafe actions and wrong-language output are rejected. No model can send, pay, book, delete or complete anything.

Learning optimises for loops that actually get resolved, not engagement: evidence builds up gradually, decays after 90 days, and any learned pattern can be forgotten. Repeated snoozes trigger a Rescue engine that offers a smaller step rather than a louder nag. Designed, engineered and shipped solo: native Swift/SwiftUI app, widgets and Apple Watch, plus an optional Fastify backend for accounts, encrypted sync and Daily Return emails.

architecture.title: How the AI is architected
architecture.summary: A layered pipeline where deterministic code always answers first, on-device models refine, an opt-in cloud model can only challenge, and one application-owned policy decides what reaches the user.

pipeline.title: Capture
pipeline.text: Text, voice, camera or scan. Exact words committed to local SQLite in one transaction before any AI runs.

pipeline.title: Deterministic understanding
pipeline.text: Dates, people, amounts, links and routines in EN/HI/Hinglish/ES/DE build a Task Frame. Always on.

pipeline.title: Action Recipes
pipeline.text: 40 versioned, signal-gated recipes propose a structured next-step candidate instantly.

pipeline.title: Apple Foundation Models
pipeline.text: On iOS 26, an on-device model refines wording from a bounded context packet. Availability- and locale-gated.

pipeline.title: Grounding & confidence gate
pipeline.text: Rejects unknown schemas, ungrounded people/times/amounts, unsafe actions and wrong language. One decision point.

pipeline.title: Local ranker
pipeline.text: Evidence-weighted ranking learned from loops you actually resolved. Decays after 90 days.

pipeline.title: Opt-in cloud challenger
pipeline.text: OpenAI or Gemini with your key and consent. Must clear the same gates and beat the local answer by more than 3 points.

pipeline.title: One next step
pipeline.text: One primary action plus at most two alternatives, saved append-only. Nothing happens until you tap.

principles.title: Commit before compute
principles.text: The thought is saved before any model runs. AI failure never loses or changes it.

principles.title: Models propose, code decides
principles.text: Strict schemas and an allowlisted Action Catalog. No model can send, pay, book, delete or complete.

principles.title: Private by architecture
principles.text: Core works with no account. Audio and images are never kept. Cloud AI is off by default.

principles.title: Learn outcomes, not engagement
principles.text: Ranking improves from resolved loops; every learned pattern is visible and forgettable.

projects.title: TheRawByte
projects.subtitle: RWA Research Studio • Onchain Data • AI Intel Agents
projects.description: A two-operator research studio for tokenized real-world assets: treasuries, private credit, stablecoins, PE/VC and real estate. Flagship reports, ghostwriting, custom Dune dashboards and AI-search intel agents, plus a free weekly Lab and a live Private Credit Map tracking 39 platforms and 98 tokenized credit assets.
projects.longDescription:
TheRawByte writes the research people read before they put money in. It covers one category properly: real-world assets onchain, across stablecoins, treasuries, non-US government debt, private credit, equities, PE/VC, commodities and real estate. Every deliverable is built on the studio's own onchain queries, explained in language that works for a TradFi allocator and a crypto native alike.

It runs as two operators with no middle layer. Ishita Rastogi leads research and narrative; Pranshu Rastogi leads engineering and distribution: Dune queries and dashboards, RWA intel agents that track competitor TVL and yield, and GEO / AI-search work so protocols surface when someone asks ChatGPT or Perplexity which tokenized treasury to use.

The free weekly Lab ships one public Dune dashboard, a query-logic breakdown and a walkthrough video, so prospective clients can check the work before paying. The Private Credit Map follows tokenized credit from issuance through DeFi to exit. Work has been cited on Ethereum.org, shared by Bankless co-founder Ryan Sean Adams and amplified by @ethereum, with clients and publications including Phala Network, Raiku, Gelato, Push Chain and Hazeflow Research.

projects.title: VANTA
projects.subtitle: AI Security • Blockchain • Transaction Firewall
projects.description: A transaction firewall that sits between AI agents and the blockchain, scoring every proposed transaction through a policy engine and AI risk scanner before it can execute. No prompt, no urgency signal, and no model error can bypass the gate — only a tiered human confirmation can.
projects.longDescription:
VANTA is a transaction firewall that sits between AI agents and the blockchain, scoring every proposed transaction through a policy engine and AI risk scanner before it can execute. No prompt, no urgency signal, and no model error can bypass the gate — only a tiered human confirmation can.

As autonomous AI agents gain the ability to sign and broadcast transactions, a single compromised or confused model can drain wallets, manipulate protocols, or trigger irreversible on-chain actions. VANTA solves this by adding a deterministic, policy-first gate that runs before any transaction hits the mempool. Every transaction is scored, analyzed for risk, and held for human review if it exceeds defined thresholds — making AI-powered blockchain interactions safe by default.
features: Pre-execution transaction firewall for AI agents
AI risk scoring engine for every transaction
Zero bypass guarantee — no model error bypasses the gate
